disasters.summary: A drought affecting parts of East Africa and the Central Sahel began on 21 May 2026. Chad, Ethiopia and South Sudan report the most detailed impacts, including rainfall deficits, delayed rainy seasons and dried water sources. FEWS NET said in August that Chad's rainy season was not yet fully established. As of 3 November 2026 the drought was ongoing, and the notes give no end date. Several sources link it to El Niño-related rainfall deficits.

disasters.summary: Drought in Central America began on 21 April 2026 and is ongoing. A 12 November 2026 water watch report shows observed deficits continuing through Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and western Nicaragua. Honduran authorities report 103 municipalities on red alert and 80 percent of national territory under some alert level. The IFRC has warned the El Niño event could last until February 2027.

disasters.summary: An agricultural drought affecting about 1,735,191 km² of northern South America and the Panama Isthmus began on 21 September 2022, according to a GDACS alert feed last updated 14 November 2026. The feed lists Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Panama, Suriname and Venezuela and rates severity as significant. Independent confirmation of its current status could not be found.

disasters.summary: Drought has affected much of Europe since spring 2026, according to the sources. In July, the JRC reported that half of the EU and UK was under drought at some intensity, with 9% at alert level. The EU Drought Observatory said drought was still critical in most of Europe in late September. Its 28 October analysis was not clear enough to confirm the current state. A forecast of a wetter November may ease the drought but not end it. The feed's start date of 21 December 2025…

disasters.summary: A flash flood struck Rasuwa district in Nepal's Bagmati Province on 26 August 2026, damaging settlements, markets, roads and hydropower facilities and affecting nearby districts. Authorities reported deaths, missing people and displaced people. The latest source found, an IFRC update dated 12 October 2026, says humanitarian needs continue and some road access remains limited.

disasters.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, on 15 August 2026 (local time), causing deaths, injuries and building damage. BNPB reported 47 deaths and 101 injuries as of 16 August, with more than 5,000 people still displaced. Aftershocks have decreased, and monitoring of secondary hazards continues.

disasters.summary: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck Colombia on 10 August 2026 at 07:34 local time, with its epicentre about 20 km from San José del Palmar in Chocó department. UNGRD's latest national balance, dated 31 August 2026, reports 16 departments and 497 municipalities affected. Deaths were reported at 335 in early September. Sources do not say whether search and rescue is still active.

disasters.title: Afghanistan: Nuristan Flood

places.name: Parun
places.impact: Flash flood; shops, hotels, homes destroyed

disasters.summary: Flash floods struck Nuristan Province, Afghanistan, from 20 July 2026, hitting Parun city hardest with shops, hotels and homes destroyed. Dozens were reported dead and over a hundred injured. Floods continued in nearby Mandol District on 22 July. UNICEF reported on flash floods through 3 August, and an IFRC aid operation was announced on 6 August. Sources do not report the situation after early August.
